messages:
Maya Chen: heads up — multiple customers reporting a big p95/p99 regression since last night's release. p95 -> ~450ms (was ~120ms), p99 -> ~900ms. All reports point to endpoints using function/tool-calling + structured JSON schema validation.

Maya Chen: example failure from cust-42: request id `req_0a1b2c3d`. They see model time still ~40-60ms but the overall response takes 400-800ms. stacktrace/latency breakdown from our side: 
```
request_id=req_0a1b2c3d latency_total=512ms
  model_generation=48ms
  router_wait=8ms
  tool_router=236ms
  schema_validation=188ms
  response_serialization=32ms
```

Maya Chen: repro steps I gave them (and tried locally):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model":"gpt-x-tool-1",
    "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"lookup order 12345 and return as json"}],
    "function_call": {"name":"order_lookup","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"include_items":{"type":"boolean"}}}}
  }'
```

Maya Chen: note — this traffic hits our tool-router and then we run schema validation on the model+tool output before returning. The validation step seems to have become much more expensive after the schema-change we merged last night (large nested schemas + heavy regexes).

Ryan Patel: looking. can you paste the exact schema they use? any sample output body that fails? also what deployment rolled last night (commit sha)?

Maya Chen: they attached the schema — pasted here (trimmed):
```
{"type":"object","properties":{"order":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"sku":{"type":"string"},"qty":{"type":"integer"}}}},"shipping":{"type":"object","properties":{"address":{"type":"string"}}}}}}}
```

Maya Chen: deploy bot shows `deploy-bot: release/1673 -> production by @ryan (sha: ab12cd34)` at 01:12 UTC. That release introduced stricter schema validation (switch to AJV with full format checks).

Sophie Alvarez: customer-impact: 3 paying customers hit SLOs, 2 on Dedicated. They asked for immediate mitigation and possible credits. I've tentatively opened support cases and escalated billing.

Leo Kim: quick hypotheses: 1) AJV full format/regex checks are expensive for nested schemas, 2) validation running synchronously on the request path rather than in a validation worker, 3) we may have lost compiled-schema caching in the rollout.

Leo Kim: can we confirm whether the compiled-schema cache was enabled? if it was disabled, compile time + validation per-request would explain the ~180-200ms.

Ryan Patel: checking logs now. looks like the cache flag was accidentally flipped in the config map for prod: `SCHEMA_CACHE_ENABLED=false`. confirmed in prod-config v3.4.1.

Ryan Patel: reproduction locally: I spun up a prod-like env and ran 500 requests hitting function-calling endpoints with that schema. results:
```
p95=470ms p99=790ms
breakdown (sample): schema_compile=130ms schema_validate=190ms model=45ms
```

Ryan Patel: so two things: compile happening on some requests (big cost) + validation cost. when I precompile schema and reuse validator, p95 drops to ~140ms.

Maya Chen: customer asked for temporary workarounds — they can disable function_calling on their integration but that breaks product. any short-term server-side mitigations?

Leo Kim: short-term mitigations we can toggle quickly: 
- flip SCHEMA_CACHE_ENABLED=true (should reduce compile cost)
- fallback: set a feature-flag `schema_validation_strict=false` to disable expensive format/regex checks (keep structural checks only)
- bypass validation for targeted customers via header `X-SKIP-SCHEMA-VALIDATION: 1` until fix

Leo Kim: I'll open a rollback PR if needed.

Ryan Patel: I'm about to flip the cache flag. doing a blue/green safe update to prod-config.

deploy-bot: release triggered: prod-config v3.4.2 -> updating SCHEMA_CACHE_ENABLED=true (canary 10%).

Ryan Patel: monitoring prometheus now. query I'm watching: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/chat/completions"}[1m])) by (le))` and per-step dashboards.

support-bot: alert created: SRE-INC-2026-0315 assigned to @Leo and @Ryan. priority=P0.

Ryan Patel: canary looks good so far. p95 down from 460ms -> 160ms for the canary shard. rolling to 50%.

Maya Chen: customers notified (Sophie sent messages). they've asked for a postmortem and timeline for a full fix.

Leo Kim: medium-term fix proposals: 
- persist compiled validators in a hot cache (LRU) and ensure cold-start compile runs in background worker, not request path
- convert expensive format/regex checks to optional plugin executed asynchronously with a warning if schema-checked asynchronously fails
- add metrics to split validation compile vs validate time in traces

Leo Kim: code snippet to use Ajv compile cache (patch suggestion):
```js
const Ajv = require('ajv');
const schemaCache = new Map();
function getValidator(schema) {
  const key = hash(schema);
  if (schemaCache.has(key)) return schemaCache.get(key);
  const ajv = new Ajv({allErrors:false,strict:false});
  const validate = ajv.compile(schema);
  schemaCache.set(key, validate);
  return validate;
}
// call site:
const validate = getValidator(schema);
const ok = validate(output);
```

Ryan Patel: rolled to 100% for cache flag. p95 for function-calling routes back to ~150ms, p99 ~280ms. will keep an eye for regressions.

Sophie Alvarez: customers accepted credit offer for the two on Dedicated, asking for timeline for the async validation improvement.

Maya Chen: action items: 
- Ryan: confirm no regressions and leave cache flag enabled (owner) — due EOD (1712009999).
- Leo: design async validation and LRU compile cache RFC — PR by next week.
- Sophie: finalize credits + customer comms.
- Maya: collect sample traces and attach to postmortem.

Ryan Patel: noted. I'll also add a short-term metric panel for `schema_compile_time_seconds` and `schema_validate_time_seconds` and add alert if compile_time > 50ms on >1% of requests.

Maya Chen: thanks all. tagging @here for visibility — will follow up with postmortem once we have root cause. :thumbsup:
